Let me think about how to structure the decomposition proofs concretely in Rocq. Example:

```
Lemma evaluates_app_inv : forall t1 t2 r v,
  evaluates (tm_app t1 t2 r) v ->
  exists f w, evaluates t1 f /\ evaluates t2 w /\ evaluates (tm_app f w r) v.
Proof.
  intros t1 t2 r v [Hmulti Hval].
  remember (tm_app t1 t2 r) as t eqn:E.
  revert t1 t2 r E.
  induction Hmulti as [t | t1' t2' t3' Hstep Hmulti IH]; intros t1 t2 r E.
  - subst; exfalso; (* app is not a value *) ...
  - subst. inversion Hstep; subst.
    + (* ST_App1 *) 
      edestruct IH as (f & w & H1 & H2 & H3); eauto.
      exists f, w. split; [|split]; auto.
      constructor 2 with x0; auto. (* multi_step *)
    + ...
Qed.
```
Hmm, the induction on Hmulti (the multi derivation) with the term being an app: the `remember` approach. So define a single relation R (call it `Rrel` or `interp`) by structural recursion on T:
```
Fixpoint rel (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      fun t1 t2 => forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        (exists k1, v1 = tm_unit k1) /\ (exists k2, v2 = tm_unit k2)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      fun t1 t2 => if sec_low_ind k then
        forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
          ((exists a1 ka1 a2 ka2, v1 = tm_inl a1 ka1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 ka2 /\ rel T1 a1 a2) \/
           (exists a1 ka1 a2 ka2, v1 = tm_inr a1 ka1 /\ v2 = tm_inr a2 ka2 /\ rel T2 a1 a2))
        else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      fun t1 t2 => if sec_low_ind k then
        forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
          exists a1 b1 ka1 a2 b2 ka2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 ka1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 ka2 /\ rel T1 a1 a2 /\ rel T2 b1 b2
        else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      fun t1 t2 => if sec_low_ind k then
        forall w1 w2 r, rel T1 w1 w2 -> flows_to k.reader r -> rel T2 (tm_app t1 w1 r) (tm_app t2 w2 r)
        else True
  end.
```
This is a clean structural Fixpoint ✓ (all recursive calls on direct subterms). Note: no need for a separate V! The relation at unit is closure-ish but with the structural result.

2. Subtyping: rel T t1 t2 → subtype T U → rel U t1 t2. Cases:

Now, the definition of R must be a Fixpoint over ty with a match returning Prop. Let's write:

```
Fixpoint related (l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\ related l T1 a1 a2)
        \/ (exists b1 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\ related l T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 kappa =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
          related l T1 a1 a2 /\ related l T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 kappa =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      forall u1 u2 r, related l T1 u1 u2 ->
        related l (ty_protect kappa.(indirect_reader) T2) (tm_app t1 u1 r) (tm_app t2 u2 r)
  end.
```

```
Inductive eval : tm -> tm -> Prop :=

| E_Abs : value (abs T body κ) → eval (abs ...) (abs ...)
```

Actually the more standard big-step: 
- e_unit, e_abs (values).
- e_app: eval t1 v1, eval t2 v2, v1 = abs T body κ, eval (tm_protect κ.ind (open body v2)) v ⇒ eval (app t1 t2 r) v.
- e_pair: eval t1 v1, eval t2 v2 ⇒ eval (pair t1 t2 κ) (pair v1 v2 κ).
- e_fst: eval t v, v = pair v1 v2 κ, eval (tm_protect κ.ind v1) w ⇒ eval (fst t r) w.
- e_snd similar.
- e_inl: eval t v ⇒ eval (inl t κ) (inl v κ).
- e_case_left: eval t (inl v κ), eval (tm_protect κ.ind (open body1 v)) w ⇒ eval (case t body1 body2 r) w.
- e_case_right similar.
- e_protect: eval t v ⇒ eval (protect l t) (protect_value v l).
- e_if_true: eval c (inl v κ), eval (tm_protect κ.ind yes) w ⇒ eval (if c yes no r) w.
- e_if_false similar.

5. Logical relation definitions on canonical terms:
```
Definition canonical (t : tm) := erase_security t = t.

Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (k : security) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  canonical v1 /\ canonical v2 /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.indirect_reader l ->
      (exists a1 a2 ka kb, v1 = tm_inl a1 ka /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 kb /\ R T1 a1 a2) \/
      (exists b1 b2 ka kb, v1 = tm_inr b1 ka /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 kb /\ R T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.indirect_reader l ->
      exists a1 b1 ka a2 b2 kb, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 ka /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 kb /\ R T1 a1 a2 /\ R T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.indirect_reader l ->
      forall w1 w2, value w1 -> value w2 -> V l T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 ->
        R l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) k.indirect_reader) (tm_app v1 w1 Low) (tm_app v2 w2 Low)
  end
```

Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (k : security) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  canonical v1 /\ canonical v2 /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => flows_to k.ind l -> (exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.ind l ->
      (exists a1 a2 ka kb, v1 = tm_inl a1 ka /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 kb /\ V l T1 (security_of T1) a1 a2) \/
      (exists b1 b2 ka kb, v1 = tm_inr b1 ka /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 kb /\ V l T2 (security_of T2) b1 b2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.ind l ->
      exists a1 b1 ka a2 b2 kb, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 ka /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 kb /\
        V l T1 (security_of T1) a1 a2 /\ V l T2 (security_of T2) b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to k.ind l ->
      forall w1 w2, value w1 -> value w2 -> V l T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 ->
        forall u1 u2, ceval (tm_app v1 w1 Low) u1 -> ceval (tm_app v2 w2 Low) u2 ->
        V l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) k.indirect_reader) u1 u2
  end.

This calls V at T1, T2 (subterms) ✓ Fixpoint accepted.

The language: locally nameless STLC with security. Key definitions:

- label: Low, High; flows_to l1 l2 := match l1,l2 with High,Low => False | _,_ => True end.

- security record: reader, indirect_reader.
- wf_security kappa := flows_to kappa.indirect_reader kappa.reader.
- security_le k1 k2 := flows_to k1.reader k2.reader /\ flows_to k1.indirect_reader k2.indirect_reader.
- public = {Low,Low}; secret = {High,High}.

- security_of, ty_protect, wf_ty.
- tm locally nameless with bvar, fvar, etc.
- erase_security: erases all security annotations to public/Low.

- multi.
- subtype with S_Trans; has_type with T_Sub.
- program contexts and plug.
- ground: Ty_Unit True; Sum/Prod ground both; Arrow False.
- transparent_at kappa T := security_le (security_of T) kappa /\ (recursively transparent_at kappa on components for non-unit).
- transparent T := transparent_at (security_of T) T.
- same_result t1 t2 := forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> erase_security v1 = erase_security v2.

Lemma V_protect_gen : forall (T : ty) (l l0 l_ty l_v : label) (w1 w2 : tm),

Now the proof of the fundamental theorem needs `V` and `E` definitions. In Coq, define them as a single Fixpoint? E and V are mutually recursive: V at Arrow references E at (ty_protect k.ind T2) which is not a subterm (T2 is, but with protection). E references V at the same T. Define them separately:

Definition E (l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V l T v1 v2

with V a Fixpoint on T:
Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => fun v1 v2 => True  (maybe if flows_to ... then True else True)
  ...
  end.

But V's arrow case references E (ty_protect ... T2) which references V at ty_protect ... T2 — same structural size as T2, which is a subterm of the arrow type. If we define V by Fixpoint and E by Definition before V, circular. We need mutual Fixpoint:

Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop := ...
with E (l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop := forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V l T v1 v2.

But in V's arrow case, we call E l (ty_protect k.ind T2) — the structural argument is `ty_protect k.ind T2`, which Coq's guard checker may reject as not a subterm of `Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k`. Even though it has the same size as T2, it's not a syntactic subterm. Coq's guard condition requires recursive calls on structurally smaller arguments. `ty_protect k T2` is not a subterm of Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k. So mutual Fixpoint won't be accepted.

Solution: define V by recursion on a *pair* (T, "protection nesting") or make V take a type and use well-founded recursion on a size measure. Alternative: define the relations as inductive propositions? Or define V with an extra parameter that makes recursive calls structural:

Observe that recursive calls in V are only on:
- T1, T2 (subterms) — plain.
- ty_protect k.ind T2 in the arrow case, via E.
- The E definition doesn't recurse; it just calls V at the same T.

So V's recursion: V l T calls E l (ty_protect k.ind T2), which calls V l (ty_protect k.ind T2) — on a type with the *same structure* as T2 (since ty_protect preserves the constructor and components). So if we define the relation by recursion on the structure of T "modulo top security annotation", the call ty_protect k T2 has the same structure as T2 < T. Coq can't see this automatically, but we can define a size function `ty_size` and use well-founded recursion (Fixpoint with fuel, or Program Fixpoint with measure, or define an auxiliary recursive function on a "structure" type). 

Simplest: define a fuel-based relation? Since types are finite, we can define a function with a fuel n = ty_size T (or a bound) and prove that calls stay within fuel. With fuel, the arrow case calls with fuel-1 and the type ty_protect k T2 whose size equals size T2 ≤ size T - 1, so fuel-1 works if we set fuel = size T. Let's define:

Fixpoint ty_size (T : ty) : nat :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => 1
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ => S (ty_size T1 + ty_size T2)
  end.

Define mutual:
Fixpoint V_fuel (n : nat) (l : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match n with
  | 0 => True
  | S n' =>
    let structural :=
      match T with
      | Ty_Unit _ => True
      | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k => (exists ... V_fuel n' l T1 ...) \/ ...
      | Ty_Prod ...
      | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k => forall a1 a2 r, E_fuel n' l T1 a1 a2 -> flows_to k.reader r -> E_fuel n' l (ty_protect k.ind T2) (app v1 a1 r) (app v2 a2 r)
      end
    in if flows_to (security_of T).ind l then structural else True
  end
with E_fuel (n : nat) (l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V_fuel n l T v1 v2.

Here V_fuel n' l (ty_protect k T2) with n' < n: allowed since the recursive call is on n' (structural). We need to ensure correctness: when n = ty_size T, all recursive calls have enough fuel. In the arrow case, we call V_fuel n' (ty_protect k.ind T2) where ty_size (ty_protect k T2) = ty_size T2 ≤ n'. Since n = S (size T1 + size T2) and n' = n-1 = size T1 + size T2 ≥ size T2. Good. Hmm, but what if n is larger than size T? Then fine. If n is smaller than size T, the relation might be truncated (True at fuel 0), which is weaker but still sound for our application if we always use n = ty_size T at the top; but the definitions E_fuel n with smaller n appear in hypotheses like V_protect lemmas (ty_protect doesn't change size). The important thing: define `V l T := V_fuel (ty_size T) l T` and `E l T := E_fuel (ty_size T) l T`. Then show that unfolding V/E at a type works with recursive calls at exactly the right fuel. In proofs, when we unfold V l (Arrow T1 T2 k) = V_fuel (size T) l ... with size T = S (size T1 + size T2), the arrow branch calls E_fuel (size T1 + size T2) l (ty_protect k T2). Let me now think about how to write V and E in Coq with the kappa parameter and the flows_to test. V is a Fixpoint returning a function tm -> tm -> Prop? Better to have all arguments explicit:

Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      (exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      ((exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\
          V l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2)
       \/ (exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\
          V l T2 (security_of T2) u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->

          E l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) kappa.(indirect_reader))

  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V l T kappa v1 v2.

The mutual Fixpoint: V's arrow case calls E l T2 ... which is a different function in the mutual block applied to T2 (strict subterm). E's body calls V l T kappa (same T). Is E's call to V on the same T allowed in a mutual Fixpoint? In Coq, for mutual fixpoints, each recursive call must be on a argument that is a strict subterm of the *corresponding* function's decreasing argument? The guard condition: for a call from f to g, the argument must be a strict subterm of an argument of f that is itself a strict subterm of ... Actually Coq's guard checker for mutual fixpoints requires that recursive calls (to any function in the block) be on structurally smaller arguments than the current function's decreasing argument. Now, the fundamental theorem. Let me write its statement:

Definition env_rel (l : label) (Gamma : context) (sigma1 sigma2 : atom -> tm) : Prop :=
  forall (x : atom) (T : ty),
    lookup_context x Gamma = Some T ->
    E l T (security_of T) (sigma1 x) (sigma2 x).

Definition lc_env (sigma : atom -> tm) : Prop :=
  forall x, locally_closed (sigma x).

Theorem fundamental : forall Gamma t T,
  has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall l sigma1 sigma2,
    env_rel l Gamma sigma1 sigma2 ->
    lc_env sigma1 -> lc_env sigma2 ->
    E l T (security_of T) (subst_all sigma1 t) (subst_all sigma2 t).

Proof induction on has_type.

I need to be careful with Coq syntax: `kappa.(indirect_reader)` works for records. In a match, using `kappa.(reader)`.

Definition:
```coq
Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      (exists (k1 k2 : security), v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      ( (exists (u1 u2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\
            V l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2)
        \/ (exists (u1 u2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\
            V l T2 (security_of T2) u1 u2) )
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      (exists (u1 w1 u2 w2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
          v1 = tm_pair u1 w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair u2 w2 k2 /\
          V l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 /\
          V l T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
      (forall (a1 a2 : tm) (r : label),
          (forall (u1 u2 : tm),
              evaluates a1 u1 -> evaluates a2 u2 ->
              V l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2) ->
          flows_to kappa.(reader) r ->
          (forall (w1 w2 : tm),
              evaluates (tm_app v1 a1 r) w1 ->
              evaluates (tm_app v2 a2 r) w2 ->
              V l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) kappa.(indirect_reader)) w1 w2))
  end.
```
Note: `v1`,`v2`,`l`,`kappa` are parameters in the Fixpoint, and the recursive calls to V must include them. The decreasing argument is T. In Coq, Fixpoint with multiple arguments: `Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop := ...`; recursive calls `V l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2` — the struct arg is T1 < Ty_Sum T1 T2 _, so accepted. But wait, Coq's guard checker compares the recursive call's 2nd argument (T1) with the 2nd argument of the enclosing call (Ty_Sum T1 T2 _) — T1 is a direct subterm. Good. The other args can be anything (they're parameters? l, kappa, v1, v2 are not uniform: kappa and v1,v2 change). Coq's guard condition only cares about the decreasing argument's subterm relation, not uniformity, for non-nested recursion. Should be fine.

```coq
Definition E (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=

```

```
Lemma evaluates_app_abs_intro : forall T body k a r u v,
  value (tm_abs T body k) -> value u -> flows_to k.reader r ->
  evaluates a u -> evaluates (tm_protect k.ind (open body u)) v ->
  evaluates (tm_app (tm_abs T body k) a r) v.

  split.

    apply multi_trans with (y := tm_protect k.ind (open body u)).
    + (* multi (app abs a r)(protect ...) *)
      apply multi_trans with (y := tm_app (tm_abs T body k) u r).
```
